protagonists.name: Inspector Aarav Deshmukh
protagonists.role: Senior Police Inspector, Crime Branch — Organised Crime & Special Investigations Unit
protagonists.personality: Observant, controlled, dry humour, stubborn, emotionally guarded
protagonists.backstory: Lower-middle-class Maharashtrian household; father worked in the municipal records office. Early-career witness-protection leak got informant Sameer Koli killed; Aarav signed a softened report — his first major compromise. Known for solving hard cases; keeps information to himself.
protagonists.wound: Fears trusting the wrong colleague again more than he fears criminals.
protagonists.arc: Starts believing the institution is damaged but repairable; discovers the same chain of command exposed a witness; final test is trusting another person with the truth.
protagonists.assignedBy: ACP Devendra Pradhan, paired with SI Naina Jagtap
gameplay: crime-scene examination and evidence handling
interviews, interrogation, warrants
police resources and case database
tactical entries and coordinated raids
official vehicle access and radio dispatch
strongest institutional records access; weakest street access without informants

signatureDialogue.hi: Mujhe kahaani nahi chahiye. Mujhe woh hissa chahiye jo tum chhupa rahe ho.
signatureDialogue.en: I don't need the story. I need the part you're hiding.

signatureDialogue.hi: Har jhooth pakadna zaroori nahi. Kabhi kabhi dekhna padta hai, jhooth bol kaun raha hai.
signatureDialogue.en: You don't have to catch every lie. Sometimes you have to notice who's telling it.

prologue.title: Call Time
beats: drive to Fort in a police vehicle
secure the crime scene
speak to Naina and a watchman
learn evidence collection and first deductions
end with the audio clue to Leela

openingVO.hi: Case file mein sab kuch likha hota hai. Bas yeh nahi likha hota ki kisne kya mitaaya.
openingVO.en: Everything is written in a case file. Except who erased what.

protagonists.name: Arjun Pawar
protagonists.role: Delivery rider, occasional courier for cash-strapped local businesses
protagonists.home: Shared rented room near the Central Line
protagonists.personality: Alert, fast-talking when nervous, street-smart, loyal, sometimes reckless
protagonists.backstory: Came to Bambai from a small town after his father Veer Pawar's medical debt ruined the family. Veer was a local reporter whose story on illegal dumping and land acquisition disappeared before publication. Arjun learned the city through delivery routes; one night he delivered a sealed envelope to a redevelopment contractor who was dead the next morning.
protagonists.wound: Resents his father's obsession with truth, but is repeating the same pattern.
protagonists.arc: Survivor who wants to stay invisible ends by choosing: remain a useful ghost, become a witness, or use his knowledge to control the streets.
gameplay: best vehicle handling and route shortcuts
bike weaving, alley escapes, delivery-timer pressure
street contacts, garages, informal safe houses
stealth through service corridors and delivery access
improvised tools and distraction tactics
weakest police-records access; recognisable by local NPCs and rival couriers

signatureDialogue.hi: Police ko route chahiye. Mujhe bas yeh pata hai ki kaunsa raasta band hone se pehle nikalna hai.
signatureDialogue.en: The police need a route. I just know which road to take before it gets blocked.

signatureDialogue.hi: Main parcel deta hoon, sawaal nahi. Par kuch parcels wapas aa jaate hain… aadmi ke saath.
signatureDialogue.en: I deliver parcels, not questions. But some parcels come back… with a person attached.

prologue.title: Last Delivery
beats: accept a late-night delivery
navigate congested roads and narrow gullies
follow a customer instruction that changes mid-route
discover a dropped envelope and a suspicious vehicle
escape a pursuit without knowing why he is being chased

openingVO.hi: Bambai mein route yaad rakhna padta hai. Log yaad rakhne layak nahi hote… aisa socha tha.
openingVO.en: In Bambai, you remember the routes. You don't remember the people… or so I thought.

protagonists.name: SI Naina Jagtap
protagonists.personality: Direct, disciplined, sharp, digitally fluent, quietly empathetic, impatient with institutional theatre
protagonists.backstory: First in her family to join the police. During a cyber-fraud case she found a seized phone accessed before it was logged into evidence — from an authorised terminal. Her complaint was reframed as a chain-of-custody error and she was transferred off the case.
protagonists.wound: Fears becoming the officer who knows the truth but keeps quiet for the next promotion.
protagonists.arc: Procedural officer who believes the right record protects people ends by learning procedure only matters when someone defends it; paths to whistleblowing, controlled compromise, or a parallel evidence chain.
protagonists.assignedBy: Partner to Aarav; her evidence-tampering case may connect to his old witness leak
gameplay: digital forensics, phone metadata, CCTV reconstruction
evidence chain-of-custody and document comparison
surveillance cameras, access logs, police database workflows
more warrant options and admissible-case building
better coordinated-operation planning
weaker high-speed street driving; police identity can trigger internal scrutiny

signatureDialogue.hi: Sir, intuition se direction milta hai. Court mein proof lagta hai.
signatureDialogue.en: Sir, intuition gives us a direction. Court needs proof.

signatureDialogue.hi: System ko hack karna aasaan hai. System ko yeh samjhana mushkil hai ki usne galat kiya.
signatureDialogue.en: Hacking the system is easy. Convincing it that it was wrong is harder.

prologue.title: Evidence Room
beats: log a phone into evidence
reconstruct a CCTV timeline
discover an unauthorised but authorised-looking access event
decide whether to flag it immediately or preserve a copy first
receive the Salvi case assignment

openingVO.hi: Main sochti thi record jhooth nahi bolta. Phir maine dekha, record likhta kaun hai.
openingVO.en: I thought records couldn't lie. Then I learned who gets to write them.

protagonists.name: Meera “Meenu” Naik
protagonists.role: Harbour operator; former BEST ticket inspector; informal logistics coordinator
protagonists.personality: Practical, watchful, proud, warm with her own people, dangerous when cornered
protagonists.backstory: Harbour family for generations; joined BEST as a ticket inspector for stability, left after a family dispute and a failed attempt to secure a traditional landing point. Now coordinates small boat transfers, repairs and cargo — some informal, some not. Once moved a sealed drum for a contractor; weeks later fish died near a stretch of the creek.
protagonists.wound: Years of compromises to protect her community; fears the truth will destroy the people she is saving.
protagonists.arc: Believes survival requires silence; ends by choosing between exposing the harbour network, a private bargain, or taking the routes herself.
gameplay: boat handling and water-based pursuits
harbour navigation, cargo inspection, manifest reading
Koli community relationships and shoreline access
undercover social access through logistics contacts
vessel types, harbour routines, cargo irregularities
limited police-evidence access; tide, weather and shallow water affect handling

signatureDialogue.hi: Samundar sab kuch rakhta hai. Bas har cheez wapas nahi karta.
signatureDialogue.en: The sea keeps everything. It just doesn't return everything.

signatureDialogue.hi: Tum log map dekhte ho. Hum log paani ka mood dekhte hain.
signatureDialogue.en: You people read maps. We read the mood of the water.

prologue.title: Low Tide
beats: move a small boat between moorings
inspect a cargo drum
talk to a boatman who refuses to explain the shipment
spot a survey mark on a concrete pillar
discover the same mark in a photograph connected to Salvi

openingVO.hi: Paani ke upar sab kuch chalta rehta hai. Neeche kya pada hai, koi poochta nahi.
openingVO.en: Everything keeps moving on the water. No one asks what is lying beneath it.
